papers.title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
papers.abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. Using a monochorionic diamniotic twin cohort (25 concordant pairs, 22 sFGR pairs), we developed a twin-specific analytical framework integrating birth weight deviation, intra-pair difference, and time-weighted variables. Through metagenomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics, and fecal microbiota transplant
papers.summary: This study uses monochorionic diamniotic twin pairs to show that selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) is associated with a disruption in the normal coupling between gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism. By integrating metagenomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, and metabolomics with a twin-paired design and fecal microbiota transplant validation, the authors identify early-life microbiota-bile acid decoupling as a potential mechanism linking sFGR to adverse postnatal growth and metabolic outcomes.

papers.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy, but resistance and immune-related toxicities continue to limit their benefit. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may enhance ICI efficacy and alleviate treatment-related intestinal toxicity, yet clinical responses remain inconsistent, and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. Moreover, clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and has not been critically integrated. This review therefore evaluates the current clinical evidence for FMT in cancer immunotherapy and examines how dono
papers.summary: This review evaluates clinical evidence for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as an adjunct to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) cancer therapy, focusing on its potential to improve efficacy and reduce treatment-related intestinal toxicity. It highlights that clinical responses remain inconsistent and that microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit, while integrating fragmented clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence on the gut-tumor axis.

papers.title: Lung microbiota in COPD: a double-edged sword.
papers.abstract: The respiratory microbiota constitutes a dynamic, low-biomass microbial ecosystem whose composition and function are shaped by continuous immigration, elimination, local growth conditions and host-environment interactions. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) provides a clinically important model in which this ecological equilibrium is profoundly altered. This review examines the lung microbiota through a "double-edged sword" framework, proposing that its biological effects depend less on the presence of individual beneficial or pathogenic taxa than on community structure, ecological s
papers.summary: This review argues that the lung microbiota's role in COPD is a 'double-edged sword,' where effects depend on overall community structure and ecological balance rather than on individual beneficial or pathogenic taxa. It frames the respiratory microbiome as a dynamic low-biomass ecosystem shaped by immigration, elimination, and host-environment interactions, and uses COPD as a model of disrupted ecological equilibrium.

papers.title: Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.
papers.abstract: Zinc (Zn) deficiency (ZnD) is a major risk factor for metabolic and inflammatory diseases associated with gut microbial alterations, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. Despite its importance, there are no established dietary recommendations for Zn supplementation in individuals with these conditions, except in cases of severe diarrhea in children. This gap stems from inconsistent outcomes in Zn supplementation trials, suggesting an incomplete understanding of Zn-mediated spatial regulation within the host-microbiome interface.
papers.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
papers.summary: This study uses a multiomics approach to map how zinc deficiency alters host-gut microbiome interactions across different regions of the intestinal tract. By profiling regionally rather than treating the gut as a single compartment, the authors reveal spatial patterns of zinc-driven host and microbial responses that may explain inconsistent outcomes in zinc supplementation trials. The work highlights the need for region-specific understanding of micronutrient-microbiome interactions in metabolic and inflammatory disease contexts.

papers.title: The ecological impact of Ulva prolifera green tide outbreaks: microbial connectivity and metabolic divergence.
papers.abstract: Green tides in coastal areas have become an increasing eco-environmental concern around the world. However, the influence of massive green tides on microorganism dispersal has not yet been explored in detail. In this study, we used amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to first systematically examine the dynamics of the microbial community among continuous microhabitats in the Ulva prolifera bloom area. We found that the phycospheric microbiota exhibited increased α-diversity and complex network topologies. The tracking of bacterial sources indicated that phycospheric microorganisms originated f
papers.summary: This study used amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to examine how massive Ulva prolifera green tides affect microbial community dynamics across continuous microhabitats. The authors found that phycospheric microbiota showed increased alpha-diversity and more complex network topologies, and traced bacterial sources to show that phycospheric microorganisms originated from surrounding environments. The work highlights microbial connectivity and metabolic divergence associated with green tide outbreaks.

papers.title: Complete coding sequence of a virus belonging to the Chaphamavirus genus identified in a pooled blood sample from Actitis macularius birds collected on the Brazilian Amazon coast.
papers.abstract: This study reports the identification of a virus belonging to the genus Chaphamavirus in Actitis macularius birds in Pará, Brazil. The genome exhibited significant genetic divergence compared to known sequences, highlighting the identification of a distinct genetic lineage and potentially prompting a future taxonomic reorganization within this viral group.
papers.summary: The authors sequenced the complete coding region of a novel chaphamavirus from a pooled blood sample of spotted sandpipers (Actitis macularius) collected on the Brazilian Amazon coast. The genome is substantially divergent from known chaphamaviruses, indicating a distinct genetic lineage and suggesting that the genus may need taxonomic revision. This is a first report of such a virus in this bird species and region.

papers.title: Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing offers superior genome resolution but is hindered by error rates of 1-15%. Existing correction methods often struggle to suppress sequencing errors without removing genuine biological variation, leading to over-correction. DADEC addresses this trade-off through a confidence-ordered framework comprising stringent de Bruijn graph (DBG) correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive DBG recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, DADEC achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmark settings while maintaining high hapl
papers.summary: DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction method for noisy long sequencing reads that uses a three-stage confidence-ordered pipeline: stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while avoiding over-correction of genuine biological variation. The approach targets the key trade-off between suppressing sequencing errors and preserving true haplotype diversity.

papers.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
papers.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.
papers.summary: This bibliometric study analyzes publications from 2008-2024 across multiple databases to map global research trends on asthma during pregnancy. It characterizes the knowledge structure, evolution, and emerging frontiers of this multidisciplinary field, highlighting shifts in research focus over time.

papers.title: Sheep or cattle fecal contamination? Using long-read amplicon sequencing for fecal source attribution and apportionment.
papers.abstract: Fecal contamination of freshwater poses a risk to environmental and human health. Accurately attributing contamination to specific sources is critical for remediation. However, discriminating between closely related ruminants, sheep and cattle, remains a challenge. This study evaluated the use of fast expectation maximization microbial source tracking (FEAST) and mitochondrial and microbial source tracking (MST) qPCR markers for fecal source identification. The focus was differentiation between cattle and sheep sources using a spiked laboratory experiment with known fecal inputs and field test
papers.summary: This study evaluates long-read amplicon sequencing combined with FEAST (fast expectation maximization microbial source tracking) and qPCR markers to distinguish sheep from cattle fecal contamination in freshwater. Using a spiked laboratory experiment with known inputs and field samples, the authors test whether these methods can accurately attribute and apportion contamination between closely related ruminant sources. The work addresses a key challenge in microbial source tracking: discriminating between fecal sources from similar animal species.

papers.title: Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving the gut-brain axis, yet genome-resolved characterization of bacterial and viral communities with metabolic context remains limited. Here, we performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling in a high-altitude cohort comprising patients with PD and environmentally matched spouse controls (living at approximately 1,900 m altitude). We reconstructed 455 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and 2,957 non-redundant viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), enabling high-resolution profiling of bact
papers.summary: This study combined deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing with fecal metabolomics in a high-altitude cohort of Parkinson's disease patients and matched spouse controls, reconstructing 455 species-level bacterial genome bins and 2,957 viral operational taxonomic units. The genome-resolved multi-omics approach links bacterial, viral, and metabolic features to variation in the PD gut ecosystem, providing a higher-resolution view of gut-brain axis components than prior 16S-based work.

papers.title: Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China.
papers.abstract: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 22 cities in China. We identified 52,314 viral operational taxonomic units, broadly representing species-level viral clusters, revealing extensive and previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, largely reflecting variation in bacteriophage diversity, whereas vertebrate-associated viruses showed a comparatively narro
papers.summary: This study performed a large-scale viromic survey of birds across 22 Chinese cities, identifying over 52,000 viral operational taxonomic units and revealing extensive previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied by city, driven mainly by bacteriophage diversity, while vertebrate-associated viruses—including some of potential public health relevance—were comparatively narrower in range. The work highlights how urbanization shapes viral communities at the human-animal interface.

papers.title: Aerobic and anaerobic cultivation shapes steroid-degrading wastewater consortia: Metagenomic insights into catabolic potential and antibiotic resistance genes.
papers.abstract: Steroid hormones such as 17β-estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) are emerging wastewater contaminants, yet the microbial communities and functional capabilities associated with their removal across different wastewater sources and cultivation conditions remain poorly understood. This study investigated P4- and E2-enriched consortia derived from dairy and municipal wastewater under aerobic and anaerobic cultivation conditions, integrating steroid degradation kinetics with shotgun metagenomic analysis. Aerobic consortia achieved >99% P4 removal within 9-12 h and E2 removal within 24 h, whereas
papers.summary: This study enriched microbial consortia from dairy and municipal wastewater on steroid hormones (progesterone and estradiol) under aerobic and anaerobic conditions, combining degradation kinetics with shotgun metagenomics. Aerobic consortia removed >99% of progesterone within 9-12 hours and estradiol within 24 hours, and metagenomic analysis revealed the catabolic potential and antibiotic resistance gene profiles shaped by cultivation condition and wastewater source. The work links steroid-degrading performance to community functional capacity, informing bioremediation design for emerging contaminants.

papers.title: Assessing dietary intake in infants through fecal sample analysis in the LLNEXT Cohort.
papers.abstract: Accurate diet tracing is fundamental to diet-health association studies, yet it remains challenging. This is particularly the case for early life studies, which rely on parental recall. Fecal sample analysis offers a non-invasive method for assessing those dietary components that have sufficient quantities of DNA remaining in stool, and are able to be taxonomically distinguished by marker gene sequence.
papers.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether fecal sample analysis can serve as a non-invasive, objective alternative to parental recall for assessing infant dietary intake in the LLNEXT cohort. By detecting DNA from dietary components that survive digestion and can be taxonomically distinguished via marker gene sequencing, the authors test the feasibility of diet tracing from stool. The approach addresses a key limitation of early-life diet-health studies, which currently depend on error-prone parental reporting.

papers.title: Diet Soda Consumption is Associated with Shifts in Gut Microbiome Function of Overweight Young Women.
papers.abstract: Low-calorie sweeteners (LCS) are consumed as sugar substitutes and may alter gut microbial composition. Their effects on microbial functional pathways and cardiometabolic physiology in humans remain poorly understood, particularly among individuals with overweight.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint examines how consumption of low-calorie sweeteners (diet soda) relates to gut microbiome composition and functional pathways in overweight young women, alongside cardiometabolic measures. The authors report associations between diet soda intake and shifts in microbial functional potential, suggesting LCS may influence host-microbe interactions relevant to metabolic health. As an observational study, it identifies correlations rather than causal effects.

papers.title: Multi-omics signatures of growth and abdominal fat heterosis in Guangxi Sanhuang × Wenchang F1 chickens.
papers.abstract: Crossbreeding can combine complementary parental traits, but whether crosses between faster- and slower-growing yellow-feathered broilers balance growth and abdominal fat remains unclear. We compared contemporaneous purebred Guangxi Sanhuang (YY), F1 Guangxi Sanhuang sire × Wenchang dam (YX), and purebred Wenchang (XX) hens, estimating heterosis against purebred group means for this single cross direction. Duodenal RNA-seq, untargeted plasma metabolomics, and cecal metagenomics used eight hens per group. YX had intermediate week-15 body weight, average daily gain, and live, carcass, and evisce
papers.summary: This study crossbred fast-growing Guangxi Sanhuang (YY) with slower-growing Wenchang (XX) chickens to produce F1 hybrids (YX) and measured growth, abdominal fat, duodenal transcriptomes, plasma metabolomes, and cecal metagenomes. F1 hens showed intermediate growth and carcass traits, and the multi-omics data revealed molecular signatures—including duodenal gene expression, plasma metabolites, and gut microbiome features—associated with heterosis for growth and abdominal fat. The work provides a multi-omics characterization of heterosis in a yellow-feathered broiler cross.

papers.title: How to train your microbe: editing environmental bacteria.
papers.abstract: Genome editing is an essential tool in microbiology, enabling researchers to assess gene function, link genotype to phenotype, and design microbes with specific features. Most tools have been developed in model bacteria, and adapting them to environmental species remains time- and resource-intensive. This review provides a framework for engineering environmental bacteria, including assessment of genetic tractability, considerations for overcoming challenges in recalcitrant systems, and an overview of techniques with guidance on tool selection. We discuss the emerging field of microbiome editin
papers.summary: This review provides a practical framework for genome editing in environmental bacteria, which are often recalcitrant to standard tools developed in model organisms. It covers assessing genetic tractability, overcoming barriers in difficult species, and selecting appropriate editing techniques, while also discussing the emerging field of microbiome editing.

papers.title: The OMM12 model after ten years: what did we learn about the gut microbiome from a defined microbial community?
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, the Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota (OMM12) has emerged as a cornerstone model for mechanistic studies of the gut microbiome. As a rationally designed, defined microbial community, OMM12 reduces the complexity of the native microbiota while preserving key ecological and functional traits of the murine gut ecosystem. Comprising twelve culturable, genome-sequenced, and phenotypically characterized strains of murine origin, the model enables reproducible and stable colonization across hosts and experimental settings. Initially developed to study colonization resistance, OMM12 has sin
papers.summary: This review reflects on ten years of the OMM12 model, a defined community of twelve genome-sequenced, culturable murine gut bacterial strains that provides a reproducible, stable alternative to complex native microbiota. It summarizes what has been learned about gut microbiome ecology and function, particularly colonization resistance, and argues that the reduced-complexity design enables mechanistic studies that are difficult with conventional microbiota.

papers.title: Integrating Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Gut Microbiome Analysis, and Structural Analysis to Reveal the Molecular Mechanisms Linking PFOA and PFOS Exposure to Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) are persistent environmental contaminants with potential adverse effects on human health, but their involvement in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), gut microbiome analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to AMD. A total of 97 potential PFOA/PFOS-AMD targets were identified, and integrative machine
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, gut microbiome analysis, and molecular docking/dynamics to identify molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The authors identified 97 potential shared targets and used machine learning to prioritize key genes, proposing a mechanistic link between these persistent pollutants and AMD. The work is exploratory and relies heavily on computational integration, so experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Complex microbial communities are found throughout terrestrial, aquatic, and animal-associated ecosystems. Genetic modification of discrete microbial taxa within native communities represents a powerful tool to study and augment microbiome functions. Herein, we develop Synthetic Phage Assisted Reprogrammable and Targetable Addition (SPARTA) as a one-step strategy for packaging, delivering, and integrating large synthetic DNA into a broad range of native microbiomes. SPARTA leverages a broad-spectrum synthetic phage particle for in situ genome engineering within complex soil, freshwater, and ma
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed SPARTA, a synthetic phage-based system that packages and delivers large synthetic DNA into diverse native microbial communities in situ, enabling genetic reprogramming of microbiome members without prior isolation. They demonstrate successful genome engineering in complex soil, freshwater, and animal-associated microbiomes, broadening the scope of microbiome editing beyond culturable taxa.

papers.title: NanoPAMDA enables rapid PAM characterization of metagenome-derived Cas9 effectors.
papers.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 orthologs remain functionally underexplored despite the rapidly growing scale of publicly available metagenomic sequencing data. Here, we applied a multi-stage computational discovery pipeline to two independent sources of metagenomic sequence data, a multi-biome collection of 620,185 metagenome-assembled genomes spanning 17 public catalogs, and raw sequencing reads from human microbiome studies assembled de novo, to identify novel Cas9 orthologs. Candidates were filtered for guide RNA architectural plausibility, sequence novelty, conservation of catalytic residues, and structural
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed NanoPAMDA, a computational pipeline that mines large metagenomic datasets (over 620,000 MAGs and raw human microbiome reads) to discover novel Cas9 orthologs, filtering candidates by guide RNA architecture, sequence novelty, catalytic residue conservation, and structural plausibility. The tool then enables rapid PAM characterization of these metagenome-derived effectors, addressing the underexplored functional diversity of Cas9 enzymes. This work expands the accessible CRISPR-Cas9 toolbox by linking metagenomic discovery directly to functional PAM profiling.

papers.title: Melon fruit microbiomes resemble aerial-tissue communities in a Turpan oasis field.
papers.abstract: Fruit-associated communities encounter belowground and aerial habitats, yet their position within the whole-plant microbiome remains unclear in field-grown melon. We profiled bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) amplicons from rhizosphere soil and surface-disinfected roots, stems, leaves and fruits. Four cultivars were sampled at fruit set and maturity in a randomised-block Turpan oasis field.
papers.summary: This study profiled bacterial and fungal communities across rhizosphere soil, roots, stems, leaves, and fruits of four field-grown melon cultivars at two developmental stages. The key finding is that melon fruit microbiomes more closely resemble aerial-tissue communities (stems and leaves) than root or soil communities, suggesting that fruit-associated microbes are primarily recruited from aboveground plant surfaces rather than from the soil.

papers.title: Xuanfei Baidu Decoction and Its Active Component Glycyrrhizic Acid Ameliorate Insulin Resistance in Type 2 Diabetes via JNK/JAK/STAT Axis Inhibition.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is driven by insulin resistance and chronic inflammation, yet current single-target therapies inadequately address these interconnected pathologies. Xuanfei Baidu decoction (XFBD), originally developed for COVID-19, is known to inhibit JNK and JAK/STAT pathways and may offer a multi-target strategy.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Xuanfei Baidu decoction (XFBD), a traditional Chinese medicine formula originally developed for COVID-19, can improve insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes by inhibiting the JNK and JAK/STAT inflammatory pathways. The authors report that XFBD and its active component glycyrrhizic acid ameliorate insulin resistance, suggesting a multi-target therapeutic strategy for diabetes that addresses both inflammation and insulin signaling.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks.
papers.abstract: The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, a
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys artificial intelligence applications across nine colorectal cancer diagnostic modalities and seven task-specific domains, drawing on 160 references. It provides a structured overview of how AI is being applied to tasks such as computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology, radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, and treatment response prediction. The paper serves as a broad synthesis of the current landscape rather than presenting new experimental results.

papers.title: OmicsNCyc: An Integrated Pipeline for Fast Analysis of Nitrogen Cycle Functional Genes With a Curated Database.
papers.abstract: High-throughput sequencing has greatly advanced our understanding of microbial nitrogen (N) cycle gene families in various ecosystems. However, current workflows for profiling N cycling genes often require multiple analytical steps, and the complexity of parameters hampers inexperienced users. Here, we developed OmicsNCyc, a powerful tool for rapid, accurate, and scalable N cycling gene analysis. With a single command, OmicsNCyc offers users full-pipeline analysis from raw sequencing reads to statistical summaries and visualization, while also supporting specific analyses of individual N cycli
papers.summary: OmicsNCyc is a new bioinformatics pipeline that streamlines the analysis of nitrogen cycle functional genes from high-throughput sequencing data. It combines a curated reference database with a single-command workflow that goes from raw reads to statistical summaries and visualizations, reducing the need for multiple tools and complex parameter tuning. The tool is designed to make nitrogen cycling gene profiling more accessible to inexperienced users while remaining scalable.

papers.title: Global biosynthetic potential of the phylum Acidobacteriota.
papers.abstract: Bacteria from the phylum Acidobacteriota are widely distributed across diverse environments yet only a few representatives have been isolated and described. Although recent studies suggest substantial biosynthetic potential in Acidobacteriota across soil and marine environments, no comprehensive cross-biome analysis of their biosynthetic diversity has been conducted. To address this gap, we analysed 19,720 metagenome-assembled genomes from Acidobacteriota along with their environmental description to provide a systematic overview of their biosynthetic potential. Our analyses reveal that Acidob
papers.summary: This study analyzed 19,720 metagenome-assembled genomes from the bacterial phylum Acidobacteriota across diverse environments to assess their biosynthetic potential. The authors found substantial and widespread biosynthetic gene cluster diversity, indicating that these understudied bacteria likely produce many novel natural products. This comprehensive cross-biome survey highlights Acidobacteriota as a promising source for natural product discovery.

papers.title: Tradeoffs in Method Selection for Analyzing Full-Length 16S Data From Nanopore Sequencing in Defined and Environmental Microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Bacteria are found in nearly every environment on earth, and the ability to characterize bacterial communities is key to investigating a variety of scientific questions. One method for characterizing and comparing bacterial communities is to amplify and sequence the 16S ribosomal RNA gene and to use these sequences (A) to determine phylogenetic relationships within and between samples and (B) to assign a taxonomic identification to each sequence by comparison to reference databases. Nanopore sequencing technology has increased the accessibility and affordability of sequencing for full-length 1
papers.summary: This study compares different bioinformatics methods for analyzing full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences generated by Nanopore sequencing, evaluating tradeoffs in phylogenetic and taxonomic analysis across defined and environmental microbiome samples. The authors assess how method choice affects community characterization, providing practical guidance for researchers using this increasingly accessible long-read sequencing platform.

papers.title: Taxonomic Guilds, Action Mechanisms, and Agronomic Deployment of Maize Rhizosphere Microbiota for Yield Enhancement: Unraveling G×M×E Interactions and Translational Barriers via Multi Omics.
papers.abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) productivity is increasingly constrained by edaphic stressors-including soil salinization, drought, and acidification-posing mounting threats to global food security. Plant growth-promoting microorganisms (PGPM) offer a sustainable alternative to synthetic fertilizers, yet despite their pronounced performance under controlled laboratory settings, their beneficial effects often prove inconsistent in open-field environments, largely due to spatial heterogeneity and genotype-specific responses. Herein, we present a comprehensive synthesis of the core microbial guilds that have
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on maize rhizosphere microbiota that promote plant growth, cataloging the main microbial guilds and their mechanisms of action. It highlights the gap between consistent lab results and inconsistent field performance, attributing this to genotype-by-microbiome-by-environment (G×M×E) interactions and spatial soil heterogeneity. The authors discuss multi-omics approaches for unraveling these interactions and identify translational barriers to deploying microbial inoculants in agriculture.

papers.title: Gut microbial metabolite indole-3-lactic acid may bind to IL1B: An in silico network pharmacology study of the gut-pulmonary artery axis in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.abstract: ObjectivePulmonary arterial hypertension is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease in which inflammation contributes to vascular remodeling. Pulmonary arterial hypertension has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis, but the specific metabolite-target interactions remain unclear. This study aimed to computationally identify key gut microbial metabolites and their molecular targets in pulmonary arterial hypertension regulation using an in silico network pharmacology approach.MethodsThis in silico network pharmacology study was neither retrospective nor prospective because no human participan
papers.journal: The Journal of international medical research
papers.summary: This in silico network pharmacology study computationally predicted that the gut microbial metabolite indole-3-lactic acid may bind to the inflammatory cytokine IL1B, suggesting a mechanistic link between gut microbiota and pulmonary arterial hypertension via the gut-pulmonary artery axis. The work is purely computational and does not provide experimental validation of the predicted interaction.

papers.title: A Multilevel Perspective on the Skin: Skin Architecture, Microbial Communities, Intrinsic Metabolites, and Emerging AI-Enabled Applications.
papers.abstract: The skin is the largest organ of the human body and harbors a diverse microbial community that constitutes a complex ecosystem. Despite advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS) that have greatly facilitated the characterization of skin microbiota composition, a critical gap remains in understanding how intrinsic metabolites mediate host-microbe interactions and maintain microecological homeostasis. This review synthesizes current knowledge across interconnected layers of the skin ecosystem, including architecture, microbial communities, metabolites, and computational analytics. The skin's
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the skin as a layered ecosystem, integrating skin architecture, microbial community composition, intrinsic metabolites, and computational/AI-driven analytics. It highlights a key gap: while next-generation sequencing has advanced characterization of skin microbiota, how intrinsic metabolites mediate host-microbe interactions and maintain microecological homeostasis remains poorly understood. The authors frame emerging AI-enabled applications as a path toward integrating these multilevel data.

papers.title: Global Analysis of Public Cheese Microbiomes Reveals Widespread Bacterial Taxa and Geographic Community Structure.
papers.abstract: Cheese microbiomes remain difficult to compare globally because public sequencing datasets are fragmented and methodologically heterogeneous. Here, we curated 14,203 sequencing records from 233 BioProjects and retained 8910 records from 112 BioProjects for standardized reanalysis, establishing a global comparative framework for cheese microbiome research. Three taxonomic profiling pipelines (QIIME2, Kraken2 and mOTUs) recovered broadly consistent genus-level patterns dominated by lactic acid bacteria, although quantitative concordance varied between methods and study collections. Whole-genome
papers.summary: The authors curated 14,203 public cheese microbiome sequencing records down to 8,910 standardized records from 112 BioProjects, creating a global comparative framework for cheese microbiome research. Three taxonomic profiling pipelines (QIIME2, Kraken2, mOTUs) gave broadly consistent genus-level patterns dominated by lactic acid bacteria, though quantitative agreement varied by method and study. The analysis also revealed widespread bacterial taxa and geographic structure in cheese-associated communities.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals the Total Yeast and Mold Species Present in Greenhouse-Grown Cannabis Inflorescences-Implications for Quality Control.
papers.abstract: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was conducted to determine the composition of the fungal and yeast species (mycobiome) within inflorescences of seven THC-containing genotypes of cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.). They were grown under conventional hydroponic cultivation or under organic production in commercial greenhouses. Up to 26 fungal and yeast species were identified from DNA sequence homologies to representative species in databanks. The mycobiome composition varied according to cultivation method, cannabis genotype, and post-harvest drying. Highest numbers of total fungal reads were prese
papers.summary: This study used next-generation sequencing to profile the fungal and yeast communities (mycobiome) in cannabis inflorescences from seven THC-containing genotypes grown under hydroponic or organic greenhouse conditions. Up to 26 fungal and yeast species were identified, with community composition varying by cultivation method, genotype, and post-harvest drying. The findings highlight NGS as a tool for quality control in cannabis production.

papers.title: The Impact of Intratumoral Bacterial Response to Vaccine Therapy in Cancer Treatment.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic Human papillomavirus (HPVs) vaccines are designed to enhance the immunogenicity of HPV and promote the elimination of tumor cells effectively. Mounting evidence implies that tumor-resident microbiomes may influence therapeutic outcomes through immune modulation. In this study, we evaluated whether the intratumoral microbiota affects the efficacy of the therapeutic HPV vaccine. We analyzed RNA sequencing data from tumor tissues of C57BL/6N female mice treated with a DNA vaccine incorporating HPV16 E6/E7 antigens fused with the chemokine CCL11. Microbial community data were acquired
papers.summary: This study investigated whether bacteria living inside tumors affect how well a therapeutic HPV vaccine works in mice. Using RNA sequencing of tumor tissue from mice treated with a DNA vaccine targeting HPV16 E6/E7 antigens fused to CCL11, the authors analyzed intratumoral microbial communities alongside tumor gene expression. The work suggests that the tumor-resident microbiome may modulate immune responses and thereby influence vaccine efficacy.

papers.title: Active temperate phages linked to core bacterial taxa dominate the wheat phyllosphere virome.
papers.abstract: The wheat phyllosphere supports diverse microbial communities, yet the viral life-history strategies that enable persistence in this dynamic habitat remain largely unknown. Accordingly, 36 non-amplified double-stranded DNA viromes were analyzed across tissues, years, and continents to test whether temperate phages are the dominant component of the wheat phyllosphere virome. A total of 7958 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) were identified, including 1211 high-quality or complete genomes, revealing extensive viral novelty. Among 726 active vOTUs, the virome was structured around a persi
papers.summary: This study analyzed 36 non-amplified dsDNA viromes from wheat phyllosphere samples across tissues, years, and continents, identifying 7,958 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) including 1,211 high-quality or complete genomes, revealing extensive viral novelty. Among 726 active vOTUs, temperate phages linked to core bacterial taxa were found to dominate and structure the wheat phyllosphere virome, suggesting these phages play a key role in viral persistence in this dynamic habitat.

papers.title: Ginseng-Douchi ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and metabolic disorders via gut microbiota regulation.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the anti-obesity effects of Ginseng-Douchi (SC), a novel functional food fermented from ginseng and soybean (both medicinal and edible resources) using Bacillus subtilis, and explored its gut microbiota regulatory mechanisms in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether Ginseng-Douchi (SC), a fermented ginseng-soybean functional food, can counteract obesity and metabolic disorders in mice fed a high-fat diet. The authors report that SC supplementation reduces obesity and metabolic dysfunction, and they attribute these benefits to modulation of the gut microbiota. The work positions SC as a potential dietary intervention for obesity, with the microbiome as a mechanistic link.

papers.title: Genomic resilience of aquatic microbes in Sangam: insights from the Mahakumbh event.
papers.abstract: The Mahakumbh festival at Prayagraj represents an exceptionally intense and temporally concentrated anthropogenic perturbation superimposed on the dynamic riverine ecosystem at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The large gathering of people during the festival can alter organic loading, nutrient availability, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, microbial inputs, and exposure to pharmaceutical, fecal, and other anthropogenic contaminants, thereby providing a valuable natural observational framework for investigating microbial community responses to environmental disturbance. This review s
papers.summary: This review examines how the massive, short-term human gathering at the Mahakumbh festival affects aquatic microbial communities at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence, focusing on changes in organic loading, nutrients, oxygen, and contaminant exposure. It frames the event as a natural experiment for studying microbial community resilience and genomic responses to intense anthropogenic disturbance. As a review, it synthesizes existing observations rather than presenting new primary data.

papers.title: Decoding the functional differentiation of herb pairs in Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang: effects on gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, and Wnt signaling in IBS-D mice.
papers.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with limited therapeutic options. Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang (TXYF), a classical Chinese herbal formula, has shown clinical efficacy, but the respective contributions of its full formula and of its constituent herb pairs, "Tonifying Tu (Earth)" (TT) and "Suppressing Mu (Wood)" (SM), remain incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to the interplay among the gut microbiota, the intestinal barrier, and Wnt signaling.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the two herb pairs in the traditional Chinese formula Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang (TXYF) differentially affect diarrhea-predominant IBS in mice. The authors examine effects on gut microbiota composition, intestinal barrier integrity, and Wnt signaling pathways, aiming to decode which herb pair contributes what to the formula's overall efficacy. The work provides mechanistic insight into the functional differentiation of herbal components in a classical formula.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium supplementation preserves gut microbiota stability and enhances wellbeing during short-term international travel: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Short-term international travel represents an acute environmental perturbation that can disrupt the gut microbiome and contribute to gastrointestinal, respiratory, and psychological symptoms. Probiotic supplementation has been proposed as a strategy to enhance microbiome resilience; however, its effects on both microbial dynamics and multi-domain health outcomes during travel remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested whether Bifidobacterium supplementation during short-term international travel preserves gut microbiome stability and improves wellbeing. The authors report that probiotic supplementation maintained microbiota stability and enhanced wellbeing outcomes compared with placebo during this acute environmental perturbation. The study links microbiome resilience to multi-domain health outcomes during travel.

papers.title: Dysbiosis of the commensal microbiota in IgA nephropathy.
papers.abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a common form of primary glomerulonephritis. Its pathophysiology remains unclear, and no curative treatment has yet been developed. Although abnormal mucosal immune responses to exogenous antigens have been implicated in the onset and progression of IgAN, the mucosal sites responsible for these responses may differ between Asian and Western populations. Furthermore, previous studies investigating the commensal microbiota on mucosal surfaces have identified multiple bacterial taxa that are significantly associated with IgAN; however, few bacterial species
papers.summary: This study examines the commensal microbiota in patients with IgA nephropathy (IgAN), a common kidney disease with unclear causes linked to abnormal mucosal immune responses. The authors identify bacterial taxa associated with IgAN and suggest that the mucosal sites driving these responses may differ between Asian and Western populations. The work supports the idea that microbial dysbiosis contributes to IgAN pathophysiology.

papers.title: A mosaic of bacterial communities and their functional potential across Antarctic moss, lichen and soil.
papers.abstract: Bacterial community composition differed markedly among substrates, whereas broad community-level differences between sampling localities were not statistically detected. The recovered U. aurantiacoatra bacterial community was dominated by Pseudomonadota, while A. regularis and soil communities exhibited greater taxonomic diversity, with Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Cyanobacteriota as dominant phyla. Functional profiling revealed distinct metabolic patterns across microhabitats. Bulk soils exhibited the broadest metabolic potential and nearly complete nitrogen-cycling pathways. The A. r
papers.summary: This study compared bacterial communities living on Antarctic moss, lichen, and soil, finding that the substrate type (moss vs. lichen vs. soil) strongly shapes community composition, while geographic location had no statistically detectable effect. Soil harbored the most metabolically versatile communities with nearly complete nitrogen-cycling pathways, whereas the moss-associated community was dominated by Pseudomonadota and the lichen community showed greater taxonomic diversity. The work highlights how microhabitat drives microbial functional potential in extreme polar environments.

papers.title: Population structure and sampling shape genomic antimicrobial resistance patterns in 30,327 Clostridioides difficile genomes.
papers.abstract: Background. Large collections of publicly available bacterial genomes can be used to examine antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but estimates from such collections may be influenced by over-representation of particular lineages and by the method used to identify resistance markers. These effects were examined in a large collection of Clostridioides difficile genomes. Methods. All C. difficile GenBank assemblies available on 20 August 2026 were identified. After exclusion of records flagged by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) as atypical or metagenome-assembled, application
papers.summary: This study analyzed 30,327 publicly available Clostridioides difficile genomes to examine how population structure and sampling bias affect estimates of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The authors show that over-representation of certain lineages and the choice of method for identifying resistance markers can distort AMR patterns inferred from large genomic collections, highlighting the need to account for population structure when using public genome databases for resistance surveillance.

papers.title: Comparative shotgun metagenomic analysis of the feline fecal microbiome in response to fresh, dry, and wet diets in a randomized crossover trial.
papers.abstract: Fresh (mildly cooked) cat foods are an increasingly popular alternative to conventional extruded dry and retorted wet diets, differing in their processing and formulation. While the gut microbiota play an important role in feline health and physiological functions, characterization of the gut microbiome in cats fed fresh diets and direct comparisons with dry and wet diets have not yet been performed. In this 42-day, 3 × 3 Latin square crossover trial, 15 healthy adult cats received commercial, chicken-based, complete fresh, dry, and wet diets in one of three randomized diet sequences. Each die
papers.summary: This randomized crossover trial compared the fecal microbiomes of 15 healthy cats fed fresh, dry, and wet commercial chicken-based diets over 42 days using shotgun metagenomics. It provides the first direct characterization of how fresh (mildly cooked) cat food shapes the feline gut microbiome relative to conventional extruded dry and retorted wet diets. The findings offer baseline evidence on diet-driven microbiome differences relevant to feline health.

papers.title: Microbial community structure and functional gene profiles of drinking water treatment plant sludge in South Africa: An exploratory pilot study.
papers.abstract: Microbial characterization of drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) sludge helps inform sludge management strategies and supports the development of disposal policies and procedures. In South Africa, the microbial composition of DWTP sludge remains poorly documented. This study characterised the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in sludge samples collected from three DWTPs in Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. A shotgun metagenomic approach was employed to provide a broad assessment of microbial taxa and functional gene categories, while physicochemical analyses were conducted
papers.summary: This pilot study used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in drinking water treatment plant sludge from three South African provinces, alongside physicochemical analyses. It provides one of the first broad assessments of DWTP sludge microbiota in South Africa, informing sludge management and disposal policy. As an exploratory pilot with a limited sample set, the findings are descriptive rather than generalizable.

papers.title: The bumble bee gut microbiota: ecological dynamics, functional roles and environmental responses.
papers.abstract: Bumble bees (Bombus spp.) are important pollinators in natural and agricultural ecosystems, but many species are increasingly exposed to interacting pressures including habitat alteration, climate change, pesticides, nutritional stress, and pathogens. The gut microbiota has emerged as a potentially important component of bumble bee biology, with evidence linking host-associated microorganisms to nutrition, immunity, and pathogen resistance. Bumble bees harbor a relatively simple and specialized gut community dominated by recurrent bacterial lineages including Snodgrassella, Gilliamella, Bombis
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on the bumble bee gut microbiota, describing its relatively simple and specialized community dominated by recurrent bacterial lineages such as Snodgrassella, Gilliamella, and Bombilactobacillus. It examines how these microbes contribute to host nutrition, immunity, and pathogen resistance, and how environmental stressors like habitat alteration, climate change, pesticides, and nutritional stress shape the microbiota. The paper highlights the gut microbiome as a potentially important but still understudied component of bumble bee health and pollinator resilience.

papers.title: Effects of a multistrain probiotic formulation on immune response and microbiome modulation following influenza vaccination in adults: a randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Seasonal influenza remains a major global health burden, despite widespread vaccination. Vaccine responsiveness varies considerably between individuals and is increasingly recognised to be influenced by host factors, including the gut microbiome. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to modulate microbiome-immune interactions, although their effects on vaccine responses and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This randomized, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested whether a multistrain probiotic formulation could improve immune responses to influenza vaccination in adults and modulate the gut microbiome. The study examines the link between probiotic-driven microbiome changes and vaccine responsiveness, a host factor increasingly recognized as variable between individuals. It aims to clarify both the immunological effects and the underlying microbial mechanisms of probiotic supplementation.

papers.title: Genome skimming of Poecilosclerida (Porifera) reveals conserved and hyperrearranged mitochondrial genomes.
papers.abstract: Genome skimming is a cost-effective approach that efficiently recovers multi-copy genomic regions, making it particularly valuable for phylogenetic research and biodiversity assessments. In this study, we applied shallow shotgun metagenome sequencing to 15 poecilosclerid sponges, successfully assembling complete mitochondrial genomes for four species and full rDNA clusters for the majority of samples, despite considerable variation in the retrieval of genomic regions and exogenous, non-poriferan sequences. Phylogenetic reconstructions using both rDNA and mtDNA sequences uncovered extensive pol
papers.summary: This study used low-coverage shotgun sequencing (genome skimming) on 15 poecilosclerid sponges to recover complete mitochondrial genomes for four species and full rDNA clusters for most samples. Phylogenetic analyses using these markers revealed extensive polyphyly within Poecilosclerida, and the mitochondrial genomes showed a mix of conserved and highly rearranged gene orders. The work demonstrates genome skimming as a cost-effective tool for sponge phylogenetics and biodiversity assessment.

papers.title: Exploratory randomized trial of the bacterial lysate Qipian in stable COPD: peripheral inflammatory, gut and airway microbiota, and fecal metabolomic changes.
papers.abstract: To explore Qipian-associated changes in clinical symptoms, systemic inflammation, microbiota, and metabolomic profiles in patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
papers.summary: This exploratory randomized trial examined whether the bacterial lysate Qipian alters clinical symptoms, systemic inflammation, gut and airway microbiota, and fecal metabolomics in patients with stable COPD. The study reports associations between Qipian treatment and changes across these inflammatory, microbial, and metabolic measures, though as an exploratory trial it primarily generates hypotheses rather than confirming efficacy.

papers.title: Effects of long-term exposure to four widely used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota plays a vital role in regulating host physiological status and is susceptible to environmental factors, including different drinking water regimens. This study aimed to explore the effects of long-term exposure to four commonly used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice. A total of 32 male mice were randomly divided into four groups and continuously administered reverse osmosis water (ROW), hydrochloric acid-acidified water (HCl-AW), sulfuric acid-acidified water (H2SO4-AW), and chlorinated water (CW) for 12 weeks, respectively. Body
papers.summary: This study compared four drinking water regimens (reverse osmosis, HCl-acidified, H2SO4-acidified, and chlorinated water) in C57BL/6J mice over 12 weeks, examining effects on growth and fecal microbiota. It provides comparative data on how common laboratory water treatments may influence gut microbial composition and host growth, which is relevant for standardizing animal study conditions.

papers.title: Elsholtzia Bodinieri vaniot dichloromethane extract exerts anti-inflammatory effects in acute lung injury mice by regulating the CCR1 and FLT1.
papers.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a disease characterized by diffuse dysfunction leading to systemic inflammation, increased vascular permeability and loss of alveolar epithelial cell function. Elsholtzia bodinieri Vaniot is a traditional folk medicinal and edible plant endowed with heat-clearing(Qingre) and detoxifying efficacies.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a dichloromethane extract of the traditional medicinal plant Elsholtzia bodinieri Vaniot can reduce inflammation in a mouse model of acute lung injury. The authors report that the extract exerts anti-inflammatory effects, potentially by modulating the CCR1 and FLT1 pathways. The work provides preclinical evidence for the plant's traditional use but relies on animal models and does not establish clinical efficacy.

papers.title: Analysis of the biological characteristics and gene function of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii.
papers.abstract: The biological characteristics, morphology, and genomic information of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii, isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women, have not yet been reported. Elucidating its biological properties and genetic functions may provide a theoretical foundation for developing probiotic preparations to treat bacterial vaginosis. The strain was identified as L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii using mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) gene sequencing. Colony morphology was observed, Gram staining characteristics were examined, and cellular ultrastructure wa
papers.summary: This study characterizes a strain of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women, using mass spectrometry, 16S rRNA sequencing, and morphological and genomic analyses. It provides the first report of the biological properties and genomic features of this subspecies, aiming to support development of probiotic treatments for bacterial vaginosis. The work is largely descriptive and preliminary.

papers.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: Drought poses multiple health risks that may affect children both prenatally and during early childhood, yet the evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence from observational studies assessing the association between drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life and child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD4202338273). We searched 18 databases and complemented the search with grey literature and manual reference screening. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed ri
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes observational evidence on how drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life relates to child health and growth outcomes. It aggregates findings across 18 databases plus grey literature, though the abstract does not report specific pooled results. The work highlights a fragmented evidence base linking climate-related drought stress to under-five health and anthropometric outcomes.

papers.title: Microbiome variation across the intestinal dysbiosis landscape is linked to inflammation and transit time.
papers.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis, an imbalance in gut microbial composition and host-microbiome interaction, has been linked to various conditions and disorders. Although characterised by multiple features, such as reduced microbial diversity and bacterial load, as well as an underrepresentation of beneficial microorganisms and an overrepresentation of pathobionts, an exact definition remains elusive. Whether all dysbiotic individuals share similar microbial composition and host properties is currently unclear.
papers.summary: This study maps how gut microbiome composition varies across different types of intestinal dysbiosis and links these patterns to host inflammation and gut transit time. The findings suggest that dysbiosis is not a single uniform state but a landscape of distinct microbial configurations with different host physiological correlates.

papers.title: The rising burden of chronic gastrointestinal diseases: the role of Mediterranean diet.
papers.abstract: Chronic gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic diseases represent a growing global healthcare burden, heavily influenced by environmental factors and the exposome. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic and preventative role of the Mediterranean diet (MD) as a potent non-pharmacological intervention in modulating gut health. A literature analysis was conducted focusing on the mechanisms of the MD-rich in polyphenols, monounsaturated fatty acids, and dietary fiber-and its clinical impact on pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), gluten-related disorders, functional GI disorders,
papers.summary: This review examines how the Mediterranean diet, rich in polyphenols, monounsaturated fatty acids, and fiber, may prevent and manage chronic gastrointestinal conditions in children, including inflammatory bowel disease, gluten-related disorders, and functional GI disorders. It synthesizes mechanistic and clinical evidence linking diet-driven modulation of gut health to reduced disease burden.

papers.title: From conventional monitoring to agentic AI: integration of data streams and computational tools for real-time microalgal surveillance.
papers.abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. Existing AI/ML frameworks can interpret these streams independently; however, human intervention is required to translate predictions into cultivation decisions, adding delays and limiting adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. This mini-review describes the transition from conventional monitoring
papers.summary: This mini-review describes how microalgal cultivation monitoring is moving from conventional, siloed data streams toward integrated, agentic AI systems that can autonomously interpret sensor, spectroscopic, and molecular data and translate predictions into cultivation decisions. The authors argue that current AI/ML frameworks analyze each data type independently and require human intervention, which limits adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. The review outlines a vision for real-time, closed-loop surveillance in which computational tools coordinate multiple data streams without constant human input.

papers.title: Potential for Improvement in the Metabolic Profiles of Patients With Hepatic Steatosis After Behavioral Change Associated With the Use of Probiotics or Vitamin E.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of changing eating habits and regular physical exercise, alone or in combination with vitamin E or probiotic supplementation, on the clinical and biochemical profiles, body composition, and gut microbiota of adult male patients diagnosed with hepatic steatosis.
papers.summary: This clinical study examines whether lifestyle changes (diet and exercise) combined with either vitamin E or probiotic supplementation improve clinical, biochemical, body composition, and gut microbiota outcomes in adult men with hepatic steatosis. It aims to determine whether these adjuncts add benefit beyond behavioral change alone for metabolic profiles in fatty liver disease.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support.
papers.summary: This paper presents a randomized controlled trial protocol comparing the Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method (a traditional Chinese mind-body exercise) against cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) in patients with sleep-onset chronic insomnia. The protocol integrates functional MRI and polysomnography to assess neural and objective sleep outcomes alongside clinical measures. As a protocol, it does not yet report efficacy results but outlines a design to test whether the traditional method is a viable alternative to CBT-I.

papers.title: Metadoon: A user-friendly GUI for amplicon analysis.
papers.abstract: The analysis of microbial communities through 16S rRNA gene sequencing plays a central role in microbial ecology and host-associated microbiome research. However, the complexity of existing bioinformatic tools often limits their use by researchers without computational expertise. We present Metadoon, a graphical pipeline designed to automate the analysis of amplicon sequencing data targeting the V3-V4 regions of the 16S rRNA gene. Developed in Python and integrating VSEARCH and R, Metadoon performs quality filtering, OTU clustering, taxonomic classification, and diversity analysis through an i
papers.summary: Metadoon is a new Python-based graphical user interface that automates 16S rRNA V3-V4 amplicon analysis by integrating VSEARCH and R for quality filtering, OTU clustering, taxonomic classification, and diversity analysis. It aims to make microbiome analysis accessible to researchers without bioinformatics expertise by replacing command-line workflows with a point-and-click pipeline.

papers.title: Species-specific gut microbiome responses to rodenticide exposure: restructuring in greenfinches but stability in pigeons.
papers.abstract: Rodent eradication on oceanic islands is essential for the conservation of endemic species. Although anticoagulant rodenticides (ARs) are widely used for rodent control, their potential impacts on non-target wildlife require careful evaluation. We focused on the gut microbiome as a non-invasive indicator of AR exposure. Here, we administered ARs to Oriental greenfinches (Chloris sinica minor) and rock dove (Columba livia) as surrogate species for the critically endangered Bonin greenfinch (Chloris kittlitzi) and red-headed wood pigeon (Columba janthina nitens) to evaluate gut microbiome respon
papers.summary: This study tested how anticoagulant rodenticides affect the gut microbiome of two bird species used as surrogates for endangered island species. Greenfinches showed substantial microbiome restructuring after exposure, while pigeons' microbiomes remained stable, indicating species-specific sensitivity. The findings suggest gut microbiome profiling could serve as a non-invasive monitoring tool for rodenticide impacts on non-target wildlife.

papers.title: Towards symbiont-based visceral leishmaniosis control: Delftia tsuruhatensis TC1 shows anti- Leishmania infantum effect in Phlebotomus perniciosus.
papers.abstract: Visceral leishmaniosis caused by Leishmania infantum is a grave disease solely transmitted by vector sand flies with a high risk of mortality when left untreated. The introduction of symbiont bacteria with anti-parasitic properties within vector species represents a promising biological control strategy for vector-borne diseases. In this context, the symbiont bacterium Delftia tsuruhatensis strain TC1 (TC1) has previously demonstrated an in vivo antiparasitic effect in the sand fly Phlebotomus duboscqi against Leishmania major, the causative agent of cutaneous leishmaniosis. The current resear
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the symbiont bacterium Delftia tsuruhatensis strain TC1 can reduce Leishmania infantum infection in the sand fly Phlebotomus perniciosus, the vector of visceral leishmaniosis. Building on prior work showing TC1's anti-Leishmania major effect in a different sand fly species, the authors demonstrate an anti-parasitic effect in this second vector-parasite system, supporting symbiont-based biological control as a potential strategy for visceral leishmaniosis.
